messages:
incident-bot: PAGE — cost-routing anomaly detected for prod-east-1 · SEV3 · routing policy sent large % to low-cost variant (possible quality regression). Pager: oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I got the page, investigating. Any quick context on what 'low-cost' variant means here?

maria (ml-engineer): Our economy routing has a cheapest-variant pool 'tiny-alpha-q4' that we introduced last month for burst mitigation. It should be gated by quality checks but looks like the policy is sending 60-80% of some customers to it.

chen (platform): I'm seeing a surge in cost-routing decisions from the policy-evaluator logs around 2078901000. Quick grep:
```
$ jq -r '.decision.reason, .decision.variant' /var/log/policy-eval/2026-03-15.log | grep -A1 'user_bucket=eco'
"cost_threshold_breach"
"tiny-alpha-q4"
```

alex (eng-sre): Support is reporting customer complaints for hallucinations + formatting regressions. Sam, did you see which tenants reported errors?

sam (support): Yep. Two enterprise tenants hit elevated error/low-quality alerts: @jess's accounts. Both triggered at ~2078901055, transcripts show repeated short/incoherent outputs. PII/formatting mismatch.

jess (cs): Confirmed. Client A reported a 15% drop in response quality for their Assist flow. They're asking if we rolled any models. We said not intentionally. :grimacing:

oncall-sre: Possible causes: policy misconfig (weight/threshold change), evaluation signal degradation, or model tag mismatch in catalog. Step 1: throttle economy routing and force traffic to standard variants. I'll apply a temporary override.

oncall-sre: Running command to set policy override -> disable economy bucket routing for prod-east-1:
```
# temporary mitigation: disable economy routing for region
redwoodctl policy set routing --region=prod-east-1 --policy=cost-aware --set 'buckets.economy.enabled=false' --reason 'emergency disable: low-quality reports'
```

chen (platform): I pushed that override and validated policy evals now prefer 'std-*' variants for sample requests. Logs show decisions favoring 'standard-beta' after 2078901200.

maria (ml-engineer): Good. Now we need to ensure no stuck KV cache / routing loop. Evidence pointed to the fallback chain: when a model fails fast, policy re-routes to cheapest variant. If the cheapest variant also returns low-quality, the feedback loop kept it preferred via cost signal incorrectly.

alex (eng-sre): I spun up a canary of the quality-checker and re-ran evaluation against our canonical prompts. Results: tiny-alpha-q4 scores ~0.62 vs standard-beta 0.91 on the regress suite. So it's not just noise.

sam (support): I've informed the impacted customers that we've applied a mitigation and are investigating. They're asking for timeline for full fix.

maria (ml-engineer): Next steps: 1) Roll back the tiny-alpha-q4 variant from the catalog for production or mark it as 'internal-only'. 2) Add stricter gating to the cost-aware policy (min-quality threshold + max-route-share). 3) Run a retro on how the policy allowed variant to graduate without sustained evals.

oncall-sre: I'm marking incident mitigated for now — economy routing disabled in prod-east-1 and customer traffic routed to standard variants. Will leave incident open for follow-up items.

chen (platform): Quick note: the policy-evaluator config had a recent PR that added a new cost_weight param accidentally defaulting to 0.9, which makes cost dominate quality in tie-breaks. PR ref: github.com/redwood/policy-eval/pull/478. Opening revert PR now.

maria (ml-engineer): +1 on revert. Also adding a monitor to track 'route_share(tiny-alpha-q4) > 5%' across regions.

alex (eng-sre): Handing off to next oncall @oncall-sre-2 in 30m — include instructions: keep economy disabled until we confirm config revert + candidate removed from catalog.

jess (cs): I'll follow up with customers with ETA: aiming for config revert and catalog change in next 24 hours, will provide patch notes.

sam (support): Logged incidents to customer tickets, flagged urgent.

oncall-sre: Summary for postmortem: cause = policy config change + insufficient gating on new low-cost variant -> large traffic shift to tiny-alpha-q4 -> observed quality regression and customer impact. Mitigation = disabled economy bucket in region, reverted policy change, removed variant from public catalog. Actions: tighter preflight evals, route_share caps, alerting on sudden route shifts, and a canary for policy changes.

maria (ml-engineer): I'll own the follow-up ML work (catalog gating + regression alerts). Chen, can you own the policy-eval revert and tests? Alex will lead the incident write-up.

chen (platform): On it. PR up in 15m.

alex (eng-sre): Creating postmortem draft and will ping for reviews. Closing active page but keeping this thread open for follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident state updated -> mitigated (2078901500). Assign: postmortem-required, severity: sev3.
